title: Ad-Free Sessions
statement:
A streaming service logs viewing sessions and the ads it plays:

- `Playback(session_id, customer_id, start_time, end_time)`: one row per viewing session; `session_id` is unique. `start_time <= end_time`, and two sessions of the same customer never overlap.
- `Ads(ad_id, customer_id, timestamp)`: one row per ad shown to a customer at the moment `timestamp`; `ad_id` is unique.

An ad belongs to a session when it went to the same customer and its `timestamp` lies between the session's `start_time` and `end_time`, **both ends included**. Report every session that has no such ad, as one column named `session_id`. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: Sessions of the same customer do not overlap
An ad may go to a customer who has no session, or fall outside every session
reference:
SELECT p.session_id
FROM Playback AS p
LEFT JOIN Ads AS a
  ON a.customer_id = p.customer_id
  AND a.timestamp BETWEEN p.start_time AND p.end_time
WHERE a.ad_id IS NULL;
brute:
SELECT session_id
FROM Playback
WHERE session_id NOT IN (
  SELECT p.session_id
  FROM Playback AS p, Ads AS a
  WHERE a.customer_id = p.customer_id
    AND a.timestamp >= p.start_time
    AND a.timestamp <= p.end_time
)
notes:
## Intuition

A session is ad-free when **no** row of `Ads` matches it. "Match" here is a two-part condition: the same customer, and a timestamp inside the closed interval `[start_time, end_time]`. A left join with that whole condition in `ON` attaches every matching ad to its session; sessions that found no ad still appear once, with every `Ads` column set to `null`. Keeping only those null rows is the classic anti-join.

## Approach

1. Read every session from `Playback` (alias `p`).
2. `LEFT JOIN Ads` (alias `a`) on the same `customer_id` **and** `timestamp BETWEEN start_time AND end_time`; `BETWEEN` includes both ends.
3. Keep rows where `a.ad_id IS NULL`: `ad_id` is never null in a real ad, so a null there means the join found nothing.
4. Select `session_id`. A session with ads never reaches the output, so several ads cannot duplicate it.

## Example 1, step by step

- Session 1 (customer 1, 1–5) matches ad 1 at time 5, the session's last moment, so it is dropped.
- Session 2 (customer 1, 15–23): customer 1's only ad is at 5, so nothing matches and it is kept.
- Session 3 (customer 2, 10–12): customer 2's ads are at 17 and 20, both later; kept.
- Session 4 (customer 2, 17–28) matches ads 2 and 3 (two joined rows, neither null); dropped.
- Session 5 (customer 2, 2–8): no ad of customer 2 falls in 2–8; kept.

The result is sessions 2, 3 and 5.

## Complexity

- Time: O(P · A) for P sessions and A ads in the worst case; with an index on `Ads(customer_id, timestamp)` each session only probes its own customer's ads.
- Space: O(P) for the result.

## Pitfalls

- Strict comparisons (`>` and `<`) miss ads shown exactly at `start_time` or `end_time`, like ad 1 in Example 1.
- Forgetting `a.customer_id = p.customer_id` lets another customer's ad spoil a session.
- Moving the time condition from `ON` into `WHERE` turns the left join into an inner join, and the null test then removes every row.
- An inner join with `NOT BETWEEN` reports a session once per ad that misses it, even when some other ad hits it.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `p` | `Playback`, one row per session to judge |
| `a` | `Ads` joined when the customer matches and the ad time is inside the session |
| `a.ad_id IS NULL` | marks sessions for which the join found no ad |

narration.1: The answer is a single column: the id of each ad-free session.
narration.2: Every session starts as a candidate, so Playback is the left table.
narration.3: A left join keeps sessions that match no ad, filling the Ads columns with null.
narration.4: An ad can only interrupt a session of the same customer.
narration.5: BETWEEN includes both ends, so an ad at start_time or end_time counts as inside.
narration.6: Only sessions whose join found no ad have a null ad_id; they are the ad-free ones.
